title: Goldbach numbers in intervals of length log² x
description:
Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we prove that for every real x ≥ r = 4.0462… the interval (x, x + log² x] contains an even integer that is a sum of two primes, where r + log² r = 6. The starting point is sharp, and 2/log² 4 = 1.0406… is the optimal constant on the whole range x ≥ 4. The best published constant was 123, due to Chirre and Hagen. Hubbard has since announced 4.45 in a preprint, and version 0.5 of this paper gave 2. The improvement comes from four changes to the classical Selberg-integral argument. We pair intervals of relative length. We use a positive-definite weight on the logarithmic scale whose width grows like √(log x). We evaluate the resulting zero sums exactly by the Weil explicit formula, which also makes the prime-power contribution negligible. And a first moment of the primes over level sets of the weight that are symmetric about x/2 doubles the lower bound that an empty interval forces on the weighted Selberg integral. The constant 1 is the limit of the method. He Li independently found the first-moment refinement and the constant 1, and posted them on 24 November 2026 as issue #1 in the GitHub repository, before version 0.6 appeared.

This archive contains the paper (LaTeX and PDF), the interval-arithmetic checks of every numerical constant in the proof, floating-point cross-checks, and a conditional Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of most of the deduction, including the new first-moment cover and the cutoff.

Status: unreviewed preprint, prepared largely with the AI model Claude (Anthropic) under the author's direction. The result is conditional on the Riemann hypothesis.
